entries.sought: For the countries and parameters no published normal gives (the WMO's sets, the 1981-2010 normals, the national services', the Deutscher Wetterdienst's and the World Weather Information Service's): the mean daily maximum and minimum temperature, precipitation and days of at least 1 mm, as averages computed from a station's daily observations by the WMO's rules

value.stations: The 25 GHCN-Daily stations of Botswana, the Falkland Islands, Kuwait, Lebanon, Eswatini, Niue, Vanuatu, Suriname, Pitcairn and South Georgia with ten years or more of precipitation or temperature in 1991-2020 (by NCEI's ghcnd-inventory.txt), each placed in the country its identifier names (FIPS 10-4, by ghcnd-countries.txt); stations of other countries near them (Cumberland in South Africa, Changalane in Mozambique, Princess Juliana in Sint Maarten, East End in the U.S. Virgin Islands) left out.
value.rules: WMO-No. 1203 (2017): a day counts where its quality flag is blank; a month's mean is none where 11 or more days are missing or 5 or more in a row (4.4.1 a), a month's sum none where any day is (4.4.1 c), a month's count of days of at least 1 mm a share of the days observed, none by the mean's rule (4.3.1 d, 4.4.1 d); a month's average is the mean of its valid values, a count's mean share times the month's days, February's 28.25 (4.3.2), where they are of at least 80% of the averaging period's years (4.4.2). The averaging period, an average as chapter 3 defines it (over any period), is each parameter's longest within 1991-2020 of ten years or more, from a year with a month of it to another, whose every month is averaged so; the latest of the longest.
value.filled: Suriname's days of at least 1 mm (Johan A. Pengel, 2009-2020) and Pitcairn's maximum and minimum temperature (Pitcairn Island, 1991-2003); the other stations' records are too broken for an average of every month by these rules, or give what their country has from a published normal.

sources.title: NOAA NCEI, Global Historical Climatology Network daily (GHCN-Daily), version 3: each station's file of daily observations ({id}.csv)
sources.said: A row per day: the station, date, latitude, longitude, elevation and name, then each element's value (PRCP in tenths of mm, TMAX and TMIN in tenths of °C) and its attributes (measurement, quality and source flag); a blank quality flag is a value that passed NCEI's checks.

sources.title: NOAA NCEI, GHCN-Daily: ghcnd-stations.txt, ghcnd-inventory.txt and ghcnd-countries.txt
sources.said: Each station's identifier (its first two letters the FIPS country code), place and name; for each element, its first and last year.

sources.title: WMO Guidelines on the Calculation of Climate Normals, 2017 edition (WMO-No. 1203, ISBN 978-92-63-11203-3), the WMO's PDF as a copy hosts it (29 pages, made 2017-11-30); the WMO e-Library's own page answers with a check this environment can't pass
sources.said: Chapter 3: an average is the mean of monthly values over any specified period. 4.3.1-4.3.2: a count is a share of the days observed, its normal the mean share times the month's days, February's 28.25. 4.4.1: a mean is not calculated where 11 or more days are missing or 5 or more consecutive; a sum only with complete data; a count by the mean's rule. 4.4.2: a normal or average only where there are valid monthly values in at least 80% of the years of the averaging period.
